text:
devon: Heads up — continuous-batcher token/sec dropped ~35% in prod starting at 17:04 UTC after the scheduler-routes merge (PR 3021). Latency SLO still OK-ish but throughput cratered, queues growing and average batch size down by ~40%.

sam: ugh. which hosts/region? any kernel fallback logs?

lina: saw it on us-west-2 canaries and then rolled to small subset of prod nodes. Kernel selector switched to `fallback_avx` for many pods around the same time. suspecting runtime chose a non-optimized kernel path.

devon: exact metric snippets: `tokens/sec` from 1.2M -> 780k, `avg_batch_size` from 16 -> 9, `queue_ms_p50` from 12 -> 48. Attaching quick profiler output (truncated):
```
flamegraph: runtime::execute_kernel -> 62%
           continuous_batcher::coalesce -> 18%
           kv_cache::serialize -> 10%
           io_wait -> 5%
```

ajay: CI perf job already flagged something on PR 3021: `ci-bot: perf/regress batch-throughput -22% on main->pr-3021`. Looks like the kernel routing heuristics change was the main diff.

ci-bot: Repro commands and perf test attached in CI job 9876. Full diff: scheduler:prefer_costly_kernel=true -> prefer_costly_kernel=auto.

maria: Can we toggle the flag to the old behavior? If we can feature-flag it, we should hold rollout. This is a rollout blocker.

devon: try a hotfix: flip `prefer_costly_kernel=false` on the canaries. Also start a bisect to find earliest commit that changes kernel selection behavior.

sam: I started a quick bisect script against the canary image tags: `scripts/infra/bisect-scheduler --range=main~20..main --target=us-west-2-canary` — first bad appears at commit `abc1234` (merge: scheduler:route-priority refactor).

lina: Confirmed locally with `bench/batcher_sim`:
```
./bench/batcher_sim --model m7b --qps 300 --seq 512 --kernel-mode=auto
# tokens/sec drops, kernel chosen: fallback_avx
```

ajay: The refactor computed cost heuristics with a stale microbenchmark that doesn't account for long-sequence KV cache hits. That pushes scheduler to smaller batches and chooses the cheaper-looking kernel which is actually slower when KV hits are high.

maria: So KV cache behavior interacts with kernel selection -> bad combo. Any idea on quick mitigation besides reverting?

devon: mitigation plan: 1) flip flag to old deterministic kernel selection on canaries, 2) force `max_batch_size=20` as temporary override, 3) backport revert of the heuristic change if toggle not enough. I'll open rollback PR now.

infra-bot: deploy halted for canary group cg-7 by deploy-bot at 17:22 UTC — flagged as rollout blocker.

deploy-bot: rollback PR created: redwood/infra#3050. Patch flips `prefer_costly_kernel` to previous explicit mapping and adds a unit test covering KV-hit scenarios.

sam: +1 on rollback. Also we need a targeted perf test covering long sequence KV-hit workloads in CI to prevent reintroducing. Filing ticket.

lina: I'll add a microbenchmark to `perf-suite` that runs seq=1024, kv_hitrate=0.65 and asserts tokens/sec within 10% of baseline.

ajay: After rollback and flag flip, canaries show tokens/sec back to ~1.15M, avg_batch_size -> 15. Not perfect but much better.

devon: marking this thread as rollout-blocker resolved for now. Follow-ups: add CI perf guard, add kernel-selection unit tests, and revisit scheduler heuristics to account for KV-hit amortization.

maria: thanks team — great triage.

ci-bot: perf/regress check: resolved for canary wave after rollback. Closing CI issue 9876.
